adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Recurrent nonpruritic angioedema with abdominal attacks, no urticaria, and an affected parent is classic hereditary angioedema with C1-inhibitor deficiency. Excess bradykinin increases vascular permeability.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Histamine, leukotrienes, serotonin, and PGD2 are associated with mast-cell/allergic pathways; the absence of urticaria and the inherited C1-inhibitor syndrome specifically indicate bradykinin.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The key remains correct even without a complement level because the lead asks for the mediator of the stated C1-inhibitor-deficient disorder, not for diagnosis from an unspecified edema syndrome.
